findings.message: A phase time in the future is dropped from the record, but it should count as unknown. After the drop, `repoPhases` is present but missing that phase. `keepRepoPhases` keeps stored phases only when the whole `repoPhases` object is absent, so the push writes the smaller object and erases the stored value for that phase. The README and the comment here say future repo dates 'read as unknown' and keep amax's value. That holds for `createdAt` and `doneAt`, which go to null and are coalesced, but not for phase times. Fix: merge phase by phase. A phase left out because its time is in the future keeps `prior.repoPhases[phase]`; only a phase the sender read as not reached is removed. Add a test row where the stored row already holds the phase that arrives with a future time.
findings.scenario: Stored FLT-301 has meta.repoPhases {proposal: 2026-10-01, verify: 2026-10-07, pr: 2026-10-08}. A developer whose clock is ahead re-raises the PR, so state.json pr.at = 2030-01-01. The push filters `pr` out, giving repoPhases {proposal, verify}. The fingerprint differs, so the row is written: the 'PR raised in the repo' history line disappears, a pin on `repo:pr` resolves to null, and an audit row is added.

findings.message: The future-date bound is enforced only by the Zod fields `PushInput.records[]`, `SyncInput.createdAt` and `TaskInput.doneAt`. Two paths skip it. (1) `SyncInput.meta` is `z.record(z.unknown())`, so `meta.repoPhases` from the self-sync (`syncSpecclaw` passes `desired()` built from `readSpecclaw`, and `phaseTimesOf` does no future check) and from any direct `sync_proposal` caller is stored without the bound or any shape check. (2) In the self-sync, `desired()` copies the unfiltered `r.createdAt` and task `doneAt` into `d`, and `repoDatesStale(cur, d)` at import.ts:101 compares them before any parse. A future date therefore always reads as stale, and every run calls `syncProposal`. That call then nulls the date and writes the same values again, adding one 'updated' count and one audit row per run. Fix: apply `notFuture` once where repo dates are produced (`desired()`, or the readers), so every path sees the same values, and validate `meta.repoPhases` in `SyncInput` with `repoPhaseTimes`.
findings.scenario: Self-sync (`pnpm --filter @amax/delivery sync:specclaw`) on a repo where state.json has verify.at = 2030-01-01 and proposal.at = 2030-01-01 with no Created header. meta.repoPhases.verify = 2030-01-01 is stored, and the history shows 'Verified in the repo' dated 2030. createdAt 2030 makes repoDatesStale true on every run, so each self-sync reports FLT-301 as updated and adds a `delivery.proposal.sync` audit row, although nothing changed.

findings.message: The repo-phase history lines changed `by` from the proposal's `source` (the ref@sha the phases were read at) to the constant 'From the repo'. The line no longer says which read recorded it. Keep the source ref (or the sha) next to the label so each phase line can be traced to the commit it came from.
findings.scenario: A proposal synced from `specclaw/094-x@9613db60` and later from `main@693b7336`. Both show 'Verified in the repo · From the repo', with no way to tell which commit's state.json gave that time.
